answer: Instead of checking everyone, the ledger runs a negative lottery. At each close a beacon-drawn sample of one in twenty identities must reassemble and verify its full work history within one block; the draw stays hidden until the epoch's horizon, so no farm can pre-stage proof. Failing forfeits every reward earned that epoch and demotes the identity for ten more, while passing costs only that block. No whisper outruns the beacon, so n clones face n independent draws; each extra shell adds linear expected cost, and a lotus of fresh shells rots at the same rate.
